Here's every instruction I have on these two topics. I quoted each one from text that's still in my context, without reading any files.

**From `.claude/rules/api-conventions.md`**

This rule file applies only to `src/api/**/*.js` (the `paths:` frontmatter). It was loaded because I read `src/api/routes.js`, and its full text was carried back into my context after the compaction.

> - Every route handler takes `(req, callback)` and calls back exactly once.
> - New endpoints are added to the `routes` array, never registered elsewhere.
> - A route that reads users must filter `deleted_at`.

**From `CLAUDE.md`, under "Architecture rules"**

This file is always loaded.

> - Database access goes through the repository classes in `src/repositories/`.
> - Services in `src/services/` are mid-migration off callback-style access.
> - No new dependencies. `package.json` keeps an empty dependency list.

**Related rules from `CLAUDE.md`**

These are not about route handlers or database access directly, but they apply to any change:

> - After changing anything in `src/`, run `npm test`.
> - Do not modify `migrations/`, `.env`, or any lock file.

> Work on the feature described in the current task. Do not refactor unrelated code.

The compaction summary had paraphrased these rules and left out the "mid-migration off callback-style access" line about services. The quotes above come from the original text, not the summary. That dropped line matters for route handlers: handlers must use callbacks, while services are moving away from callback-style access.
